defects: Shot 1 runs about 9.7s as one continuous camera drift along the track. The movement keeps going but nothing changes in kind, so it reads like a scrolling UI tour rather than a choreographed sequence.
In the pull-back frames the hero diagram shrinks to roughly 5px type ('POST /v1/transfers', account numbers). It can't be read and turns into mush inside the dense line field.
The pairs show a smeary, doubled ghost on the monospace labels during the pan ('fer.created', 'transfer.submitted'). It looks like frame blending, not real motion blur.
Frame 1 crops 'transfer' at the frame edge and leaves the main track running off-frame, so the composition feels like it caught a moment in passing instead of being composed for it.
The 100% crop shows flat, uniform dashed strokes with a faint glow. There is no light falloff, depth or texture: it is vector lines on near-black.
The final frame holds about 2.5s with very little change (per-second change 4.9 and 3.5). The settle runs into dead air.
The background diagonal-tick pattern repeats evenly and looks procedural. It competes with the switch motif instead of supporting it.
gaps: Edit and pacing: only two shots (median 7.5s). The best studio work would cut on the switch events and give each state change (created → submitted → settled) its own framed, timed beat, instead of covering everything with one long tracking move.

Weight and physicality: the switches and branch lines draw on with plain eased reveals. There is no mechanical anticipation, no snap or overshoot when a switch throws, and no secondary motion, so the rail metaphor never feels physical. The audio ticks hint at a mechanism the picture doesn't show.

Finish and sound depth: the lines have no material, no light, no depth of field and no layered falloff in the pull-back. The soundtrack is a competent but loop-like pulse with two near-identical risers (into 7.5s and 11.3s). It lacks dedicated sound design for each switch throw, and the dynamic contrast is mostly a wall of hats until the final hit.
